node.title: Re^8: Selecting Ranges of 2-Dimensional Data
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I checked CPAN, and it seemed like there were no [cpan://Tie::] modules that cover this niche (BTW, it's interesting how many different Tie::* modules there are), so I just released [dist://Tie-Subset]. My code from [id://1224800|here] now has two more working implementations:

use Tie::Subset::Array; sub arr_alias_4 { my ($arr,@i) = @_; tie my @x, 'Tie::Subset::Array', $arr, \@i; return \@x; } use Tie::Subset::Hash; sub hash_alias_4 { my ($hash,@k) = @_; tie my %x, 'Tie::Subset::Hash', $hash, \@k; return \%x; }

[id://1224765|Earlier] you said:

@_ ... seems to be reliable. Though not many people know if it depends on an implementation detail.

I've included [https://github.com/haukex/Tie-Subset/blob/master/t/80_alias.t|a test] in the above distribution that tests it. So it'll be run on [http://matrix.cpantesters.org/?dist=Tie-Subset%200.01|CPAN Testers] and now we have a canary to see if one of the newer releases of Perl starts breaking the aliasing via \@_ :-)
